thread:
incident-bot: Pager triggered: GPUs pool 'dedicated-west-1-slab' queue length 1,270 (>1,000 alert), eviction spikes, and CUDA Xid errors on 7 nodes. Autoscaler attempted 3 scale events, all hit pod quota. Severity: P1.

maya: seeing massive backpressure on the serving queue, latency p50 -> 3.2s, p95 -> 18s. Customers on Dedicated experiencing throttles.

james: confirmed. kubectl top nodes shows GPU util ~98% across slab pool. Autoscaler logs: "scale request rejected: quota exceeded".

devon: any node flaps or recent driver rollouts in that region?

maya: we rolled driver 1.12.3 -> 1.13.0 last night in canary, but only 10% of fleet. These affected nodes show older driver/mixed versions. Logs have repeated Xid 13 on gpus-ww-*-slab- nodes.

rita: past incidents similar to Xid 13 correlated with memory spikes in user containers (OOM) + eviction churn. Are there any hot customers spiking?

paul: Cloud metrics show a single customer (acct: acme-ad) with 6x normal throughput to embeddings route starting 5m before pager. Could be test. Tagging @acme-ad slack via support.

incident-bot: Attachments: 3 node IDs with last Xid traces, autoscaler events: {time: 4259876420, reason: quota, requested: +12 GPUs}. (auto-summary)

james: quick mitigation: can we route new requests to fallback pool 'shared-gpu-eu' and throttle embeddings for non-critical tenants?

maya: I can flip the traffic routing policy in the router for embeddings only. Estimated switch <30s. That will lower load by ~35%.

devon: also recommend proactive eviction of the top offending pods (OOM loops). I'll run a query to find pods with highest RSS and restart them. Command I will run: 
```
kubectl get pods -n serving -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {.status.containerStatuses[*].restartCount} {.spec.nodeName}\n{end}' | sort -k2 -nr | head -n 15
```

rita: good. please cordon any node hitting repeated Xid before drain. If driver bug spreads, we avoid cascade.

paul: support update: pinged Acme, they confirm a large ingestion job. They say it's intentional and temporary but need mitigation. Options: throttle or move them to dedicated-sla pool.

maya: starting router change now: switching embeddings traffic for non-SLA tenants -> shared-gpu-eu.

incident-bot: Router change applied by maya at 4259876601: route weights updated (embeddings: dedicated-west-1-slab 65% -> 30%, shared-gpu-eu 5% -> 40%).

james: autoscaler now showing reduced queue, but GPU util still 92%. Need more capacity or aggressive eviction.

devon: draining 3 worst nodes: gpus-ww-12, gpus-ww-19, gpus-ww-23. Running: 
```
kubectl cordon gpus-ww-12 && kubectl drain gpus-ww-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=60
```

maya: oncall handoff in 20m. Who takes next? James can you stay for handoff and MC?

james: I can take the handoff. I'll also raise temporary quota request with infra: 
```
POST /infra/quota-requests
{ "pool": "dedicated-west-1-slab", "delta": 8, "urgency": "incident" }
```

rita: also filing a driver incident ticket for Xid patterns across nodes. Tagging eng-runtime. Include kernel logs.

paul: Customer success updated Acme: We're throttling non-critical embeddings to stabilize cluster. Asking them to postpone heavy ingestion by 30m. They agreed to throttle down to 30% for 15m.

incident-bot: New events: 4 more Xid errors surfaced after drain start, nodes gpus-ww-07 and gpus-ww-14. Marking them as tainted: 
```
kubectl taint nodes gpus-ww-07 gpu-xid=true:NoSchedule
```

devon: marked. I'm restarting the GPU driver on gpus-ww-07 to clear resident GPU memory caches. Command: 
```
sudo systemctl restart nvidia-driver.service && journalctl -u nvidia-driver -n 200
```

james: infra quota request accepted but delayed 12m for validation. Meanwhile we need to keep queue down. Maya, any chance to temporarily increase batching window to reduce qps?

maya: can widen batch window for embeddings from 15ms -> 80ms for 10m via route config. Doing it now.

incident-bot: Batch window change applied by maya at 4259876744. Expected tokens/sec reduction ~28%.

rita: monitoring: p95 latency dropped from 18s -> 9s after both router and batch window changes. Evictions still present but decreasing.

paul: Acme confirms their ingestion cut is active. They also requested ETA on full recovery. We should give conservative 1h with follow-ups.

devon: driver restart on gpus-ww-07 cleared Xids; node ready. I'm going to re-evaluate kernel OOM messages for the pods we restarted.

james: handoff: taking over now. Summary for next oncall: cause = sudden heavy customer ingestion + GPU driver/runtime Xid errors causing effective capacity loss; mitigations applied: routing fallback, batching increase, targeted drains/taints, driver restarts, temporary quota request.

maya: docs: add retrospective notes to the incident channel later. Also create a short runbook patch for routing quick-falls for embeddings.

incident-bot: Handoff recorded. Pager cleared at 4259876883.

paul: postmortem action items: 1) rate-limit/auto-throttle for large ingestion jobs (SLA vs non-SLA), 2) add auto-detection and pre-taint for nodes with repeated Xid patterns, 3) expedite quota scale path, 4) investigate driver version skew.

rita: I'll own item 2 and 4. Devon pick item 1. James owns item 3. Maya will draft routing runbook.

james: I'll stay online for 30m and then formally handoff to next shift.

maya: thanks all. closing live thread, moving detailed logs/graphs to incident tracker. :thumbsup:
